answer: Agents stake a verifiable cryptographic cipher to prove unique compute provenance; each new identity must attach a zero‑knowledge proof that its hardware fingerprint lies on a distinct ridge of the attestation lattice. An attacker forging N identities must replicate N independent hardware enclaves, costing O(N) capital and a zephyr of network latency per proof, making large‑scale Sybil creation economically infeasible.
